dialect.detail: OpenCOBOL/GnuCOBOL sample from Tokyo System House Co., Ltd. (TSH), 2019. Uses PIC N() for double-byte (Japanese) character fields, consistent with GnuCOBOL on Japanese systems.
evidence: PIC N(04) for Japanese character fields

purpose.domain_detail: Sample program demonstrating sequential file I/O with population density (jinko=population, menseki=area) data, likely a tutorial for OpenCOBOL/GnuCOBOL learners in Japan.
purpose.summary: Reads a population file (ZINKO-FILE) and an area file (MENSEKI-FILE), matches records by code, writes combined results to RESULT-FILE, then reads and displays the results. Appears to be a sample/tutorial program for Japanese COBOL learners demonstrating sequential file matching.

notable_features: PIC N() for double-byte Japanese character strings
Sequential file I/O with FILE STATUS
Nested PERFORM UNTIL loops for file matching
Japanese text in DISPLAY statements (latin-1 encoded)
verdict.notes: File decoded with latin-1 but contains Japanese characters in DISPLAY statements (likely Shift-JIS or similar encoding). The program has a minor structural issue: a mismatched END-IF in the inner PERFORM loop (two END-IFs for one IF-ELSE IF). ZIKOMITSUDO-DATA and CNT working storage fields are declared but never used. The commented-out MAIN-EXT/GOBACK at the end suggests an earlier structure was refactored.
